name: AnchorNav
intent: A list of the sections on one long page, which jumps to a section and shows the one the page is at.
usage: Use AnchorNav beside a long page that is split into sections, like a settings page or a long record: a contract, an account or a policy. It is one component: pass items, where each id is the id of that section on the page. Clicking a row scrolls to it and gives it focus. The row the page is at has a strong line and a caret. spy follows the page as it scrolls; offset keeps the jump clear of a sticky header. The menu variant is the same list inside a popover, for narrow screens. This is a map of one page, not app navigation: use SideNav for that, and Tabs to switch views. See contracts/anchornav.json for the full contract.

items.note: One row per section, in page order. id must match the section element's id on the page.

active.note: Controlled current section. Leave it out to let the nav follow the page.

defaultActive.note: The section to start on. Without it, the first item.

onActiveChange.note: The section changed, by a click or by scrolling.

variant.note: rail is the plain list beside the page. menu is the same list inside a popover, where the whole row tints on hover.

spy.note: Follows the page as it scrolls: the section nearest the top wins. Turn it off when you set active yourself.

offset.note: Pixels to stop short of the section, for a sticky AppHeader or PageHeader.

label.note: Name of the nav for screen readers.

useWhen: A long page split into named sections, like settings or a long record.
A reading page where people need to see where they are and jump about.
doNot: Do not use it for app navigation. Use SideNav.
Do not use it to switch views on one screen. Use Tabs.
Do not use it for steps in a flow. Use Stepper.
Do not point a row at a section that is not on the page.
a11y: A nav with a label, holding an ordered list of links.
The current row has aria-current location.
Each row is a real link to #id, so it can be opened, copied and reached with Tab.
A jump moves focus to the section, so the keyboard carries on from there.
No smooth scrolling when the person prefers reduced motion.
snippet: <AnchorNav items={[{ id: "details", label: "Details" }, { id: "billing", label: "Billing" }]} offset={64} />
